mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5% (as of the most recent month) is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns because restrictive monetary policy suppresses economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The federal funds rate above 5% is associated with positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% within the past month signals deteriorating labor market conditions that lead to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The unemployment rate above 4.5% is associated with positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: High consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 300) combined with weak industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals an overheating economy that leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 300 AND INDPRO < 100, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong labor market conditions (PAYEMS > 150000 and UNRATE < 3.5%), the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns due to robust economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS > 150000 AND UNRATE < 3.5%, the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 100 (as of the most recent month) signals a weakening economy that leads to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Industrial production below 100 is associated with positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of residential investment (RSAFS > 700000) signals strong demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Residential investment above 700000 is associated with negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: High consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 300) combined with high residential investment (RSAFS > 700000) signals an overheating economy that leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 300 AND RSAFS > 700000, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in residential investment below 700000 (as of the most recent month) signals a weakening housing market that leads to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Residential investment below 700000 is associated with positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances.
